assign.brief: The swipe-up chat sheet on a phone becomes a page at full height: routed, with a back button, and the OS back button always works

steps: find the sheet: ext/drawer/rail.js DrawerRailSheetPanel, resized by ext/grip axis y
route the sheet: ?sheet=open|full, a history entry per step, Back button at full
fix the drag: height not only a cap; snap to full / close on release; grip bugs
prove: headless phone shots at each height + after history.back()

decision.what: The sheet's state lives in the url as ?sheet=open or ?sheet=full, each step a pushed history entry, so OS back steps full -> open -> closed and never leaves the site. A url loaded straight at ?sheet=full rebuilds the two entries under it.
decision.alternative: pushState with the same url and only history.state changed: back works, but a reload or a shared link would lose the sheet (CLAUDE.md: route everything).

decision.what: core/Router: a popstate that stays on the same path no longer reloads the page. Without it every sheet back step scrolled the page behind to the top and fired navigated().
decision.alternative: leave Router alone and let the sheet's back steps reload the same page each time (scroll jump, a redundant navigated()).

log.msg: jank found: the sheet had only max-block-size from --sheet-h, so dragging above its content height did nothing (the finger moved, the sheet did not). Also grip.js kept the last drag's size, so a plain tap on the grip re-fired done() with a stale size, and it had no pointercancel, which can leave the whole page in resize mode.
